questions.question: Which technique is used when the nurse listens to breath sounds with a stethoscope?
choices: Inspection
Palpation
Percussion
Auscultation
questions.explanation: Auscultation is listening to body sounds with a stethoscope. Inspection uses observation, palpation uses touch, and percussion uses tapping to assess underlying tissue.

questions.question: Which sequence is correct for a routine abdominal assessment?
choices: Inspect, auscultate, percuss, palpate
Inspect, palpate, percuss, auscultate
Palpate, inspect, auscultate, percuss
Auscultate, percuss, palpate, inspect
questions.explanation: The abdomen is assessed by inspection, auscultation, percussion, then palpation. Palpation and percussion can change bowel sounds and may increase discomfort, so auscultation occurs first.

questions.question: A client reports severe right-lower-quadrant abdominal pain. Which action is appropriate during the physical assessment?
choices: Palpate the painful area first to confirm the report
Assess nonpainful areas first and palpate the painful area last if appropriate
Avoid asking about the pain to prevent anxiety
Give the client food before continuing the assessment
questions.explanation: Painful areas are assessed last to reduce discomfort and guarding while allowing comparison with less painful areas. The RN continues to assess urgency and follows the escalation plan for concerning findings.

questions.question: During a respiratory assessment, which finding is the highest priority?
choices: A dry cough reported for two days
New accessory-muscle use with short phrases during speech
A request for a second pillow
Mild nasal congestion with normal effort
questions.explanation: Accessory-muscle use and inability to speak in full phrases suggest increased work of breathing and possible deterioration. The RN should immediately assess airway, breathing, oxygen delivery, vital signs, and need for help.

questions.question: While assessing an older adult, the RN notes new facial asymmetry, right arm drift, and slurred speech. What is the priority action?
choices: Complete the rest of the head-to-toe assessment
Offer oral fluids and reassess in one hour
Activate the facility's urgent neurologic-response process while protecting the client
Document the findings at the end of the shift
questions.explanation: New focal neurologic deficits are time-sensitive cues. The RN protects the client, notes onset or last-known baseline when possible, performs focused assessment, and activates the required urgent response.

questions.question: Which skin-assessment approach is best for detecting possible early pressure-related injury across different skin tones?
choices: Assess only for visible redness
Compare with surrounding skin and assess color change, temperature, texture, tenderness, and nonblanching change
Skip the skin assessment if the client denies pain
Massage every bony prominence to improve circulation
questions.explanation: Redness alone may not reveal early change across all skin tones. Comparing areas and assessing multiple visual and tactile cues supports more equitable detection. Massage over vulnerable tissue can cause harm.

questions.question: During assessment of an IV site, the RN notes swelling, coolness, and new discomfort above the insertion site. What should the RN do first?
choices: Ignore the finding if the infusion pump has no alarm
Stop the infusion and assess the site and client according to the organization's IV complication process
Increase the infusion rate to check patency
Cover the site so the client cannot touch it
questions.explanation: Swelling, coolness, and discomfort may indicate an IV complication. The RN stops the infusion, assesses, protects the client, and follows organizational policy for the medication or solution involved and required notification.

questions.question: Which action best supports accurate comparison of lung sounds?
choices: Listen only to the most symptomatic side
Auscultate comparable areas side-to-side in a systematic pattern
Place the stethoscope over clothing to preserve privacy
Ask the client to hold the breath throughout the assessment
questions.explanation: A systematic side-to-side comparison helps identify asymmetry and localize unexpected sounds. Auscultation is generally performed on skin in a quiet environment, while the client breathes as directed.

questions.question: Which documentation entry best communicates an important assessment change?
choices: Client has abnormal lungs and needs watching
Client seems weaker than usual
At 1840, respirations 30/min with accessory-muscle use; oxygen device intact at ordered setting; rapid-response process activated
Head-to-toe assessment completed, no further details needed
questions.explanation: The entry gives the time, specific objective cues, relevant treatment context, and nursing action. Vague labels do not let the next clinician understand severity, trend, or response.

questions.question: After the RN reports new unilateral lower-extremity coolness and a weaker pulse than the opposite side, what action is essential next?
choices: Assume the report completes the assessment
Reassess the client and document the response to the escalation plan
Wait until routine vital signs are due
Massage the affected extremity vigorously
questions.explanation: Escalation does not end nursing accountability. The RN continues focused assessment, protects the client, follows the response plan, documents communications and actions, and evaluates the client's condition.
